basic_identification.full_title: Pliers and Nippers for Electronics — Technical Supply Conditions
basic_identification.sector_category: Production Engineering / Assembly Hand Tools (finalized by the Assembly Hand Tools Sectional Committee PE 05 and approved by the Production Engineering Division Council of the Bureau of Indian Standards) [1]

scope.summary: This standard specifies the technical supply conditions for pliers and nippers for electronics used manually for gripping and cutting while working on electronic gadgets [2]. It explicitly excludes tools intended for working on live electrical circuits and antistatic applications [2].

requirements.detail: Tools must be made from high-quality carbon or alloy steels [4]. Suitable tool steel examples conforming to IS 3749 : 1978 include grades 65T6, 70T3, and 75T6 [4]. Rivets must conform to IS 2155 : 1982 [4].

For insulated variants, sleeves or insulating materials must cover the entire handle including the outer shoulder [4]. Materials must withstand high-voltage insulation tests per Clause 8.5, but the test voltage must not be printed on the tool or insulation [4]. Completed insulation is not a absolute guarantee of safety against subsequent mechanical damage, liquids, or perspiration [4].

Tools must carry differential heat treatment hardness. The main tool body must hold a hardness of 350 to 510 HV (~35 to 50 HRC) [4]. The wear-intensive cutting edges must be separately hardened to a range of 510 to 700 HV (~50 to 60 HRC) [4].

Pliers and nippers must be solid forged to shape [4]. Joint rivets must carry an interference fit in one of the tool arms and a free fit in the other, finished completely flush with the surrounding surfaces [4]. Gripping jaws and cutting blades must be hardened and tempered cleanly, and any serrations must be neatly cut to ensure firm gripping [4].

requirements.requirement_type: Flat Nose and Snipe Nose Load Test
requirements.detail: Requires applying test load F8, calculated per formulae in Tables 2 and 3 [7]. Jaws must grip a 3 mm thick test piece over a length of 2 mm from the tip [7]. The test piece hardness must be between 40 HRC and 40 HRC [7]. Upon load release, the tool must show zero damage affecting its mechanical operation [7].
Pliers are designated per IS 13610 : 1992 in the following order: shape of nose (end view), shape of nose (longitudinal), presence of serrations, and presence of grooves [6].
Nippers are designated per IS 13610 : 1992 in the following order: direction and position of cutting edges, type and shape of cutting edges, and the specific field of application [6].

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 13636 : 1993 is the national Indian Standard specification governing technical supply conditions for manual gripping and cutting pliers and nippers designed specifically for electronic assembly work, such as on printed circuit boards and electronic components [1, 2, 5]. Drawing dimensional and testing blueprints from ISO 9656 and ISO 9657, the standard outlines requirements for raw materials, specifying tool steel grades like 65T6 and 70T3 [4, 5]. It enforces a dual-hardness heat treatment scheme where the main tool body carries a hardness of 350 to 510 HV while the high-wear cutting edges are hardened to 510 to 700 HV to prevent dulling [4]. Furthermore, the standard outlines mechanical load testing limits (such as the tip-gripping load test on a 40 HRC hardened test piece), defines strict flush joint rivet assembly rules, and prescribes detailed designation sequences based on nose geometries to streamline industrial procurement [4, 6, 7].
